title: The sequential isolation of metabolites, RNA, DNA, and proteins from a single, undivided mixed microbial community sample
protocol: Collect sample in a sterile tube and immediately snap-freeze it in liquid nitrogen.
Preserve the sample at -80 °C until pre-processing.
With a sterile spatula, reduce the sample to powder form or very small pieces around 200 mg +/- 10 % of frozen sample.
Cool down all equipment and refreeze regularly the material by briefly dipping it into liquid nitrogen.
Float a weighing boat on the surface of the liquid nitrogen and pour the powdered sample into this.
Transfer the frozen sample into a pre-cooled 2 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Refreeze the 2 ml microcentrifuge tube briefly in a liquid nitrogen bath.
Thaw the sample on ice for approximately 10-15 minutes by placing the sample tube horizontally on the ice surface.
Flip the tube regularly and verify the consistency of the sample every few minutes.
Centrifuge the thawed samples at 18,000 × g for 15 minutes at 4 °C.
Transfer the supernatant into a fresh 2 ml sterile tube pre-cooled to 4 °C.
If visible particles are still present in the supernatant, carry out an additional centrifugation for 5 minutes until a completely limpid supernatant is obtained.
Proceed to step B.4 with the supernatant.
Snap-freeze the cell pellet and preserve it at -80 °C until step C.2.
Add one volume of the aqueous supernatant from step B.2 to one volume of cold methanol (at -20 °C) and two volumes of cold chloroform (at -20 °C).
Vortex the mixture thoroughly.
Mix the supernatant and solvents by placing the tube in a shaker set to maximum speed for 30 minutes at 4 °C.
Centrifuge the mixture at 14,000 × g and 4 °C for 5 minutes.
Transfer the polar (top) phase into a separate 2 ml tube.
Transfer the non-polar (lower) phase into another separate 2 ml tube.
Aliquot extracellular polar and non-polar metabolite fractions into glass vials, typically using a volume of 70 μl.
Dry polar metabolite fractions in a vacuum centrifuge.
Dry non-polar metabolite fractions under a chemical hood.
Cap tubes and preserve them at -80°C until further analysis.
Cool nucleic acid-free milling balls by dipping the microcentrifuge tubes containing them in liquid nitrogen.
Add cold milling balls to previously obtained frozen cell pellet.
Cryomill the frozen pellet for 2 min at 25 Hz using a Retsch Mixer Mill MM 400.
Dip the tube immediately in liquid nitrogen after cryomilling to preserve the sample in a frozen state.
Sequentially add 300 μl of cold methanol:water (1:1; v/v) and 300 μl of cold chloroform to the pulverised sample.
Vortex the mixture until complete dissolution.
Mill the sample tube for an additional 2 min at 20 Hz in the Retsch Mixer Mill MM 400.
Wrap Parafilm around the rim of the cap of the sample tube before starting the milling.
Remove Parafilm before proceeding to the next step.
Centrifuge the sample tube at 14,000 × g and 4 °C for 5 min.
Transfer the polar phase into a new 2 ml tube.
Transfer the non-polar phase into a new 2 ml tube.
Preserve the interphase with milling beads in the original tube on ice.
Proceed immediately to section D.
Aliquot the intracellular polar and non-polar metabolites in glass vials as described in step B.8.
Add 10 μl of 2-β-mercaptoethanol to each ml of RLT buffer (Qiagen) to prevent RNA degradation during cell lysis.
Add 600 µl of cold (4 °C) modified RLT buffer to the interphase pellet from step C.9.
Cover the rim of the closed tube cap with Parafilm to avoid leakage.
Resuspend the interphase in the modified lysis buffer by a quick vortexing of the sample tube.
Mill the sample for 30 sec at 25 Hz using the Retsch Mixer Mill MM 400.
Ensure that the adaptor racks are pre-cooled to 4 °C before the milling step.
Transfer up to 700 μl of the lysate into a QIAshredder column.
Centrifuge for 2 min at maximum speed and at room temperature.
Check the quantity and quality of the RNA fraction using the Agilent Bioanalyzer 2100 with the 6000 Nano RNA kit.
Check the size and quality of the DNA fraction by agarose gel electrophoresis.
Quantify extracted DNA using Thermo Scientific NanoDrop 2000c.
Quantify extracted RNA using Agilent Bioanalyzer 2100 with the 6000 Nano RNA kit.
Quantify extracted proteins using Life Technologies Qubit 2.0 fluorometer with the Qubit Protein Assay kit.
Precipitate RNA using ethanol.
Overlay the RNA pellet with Ambion RNAlater solution.
Ship the sample containing RNAlater to the sequencing facility on dry ice.
Precipitate protein fraction using TCA.
